## Disposition and attribution

Accept a complete, credited prior counterexample for 30000977 / OWR-1971-010. The bound degree <= 4 is false: the Gleissner–Pignatelli–Rito surface has exactly nine A2 canonical singularities, Cartier ample base-point-free K, K squared 24, pg=4, and complete canonical morphism of degree 12 onto a singular rank-three quadric cone in P3. The image has degree 2, hence minimal degree. The degree-27 construction cover onto P1 x P1 is a distinct map.

Credit: Christian Gleissner, Roberto Pignatelli and Carlos Rito, *New surfaces with canonical map of high degree*, Communications in Analysis and Geometry 30(8) (2022), 1811–1823, [DOI](https://doi.org/10.4310/cag.2022.v30.n8.a5). The contextual patch clarifies the inverse-eigenline convention and records independent acceptance; no mathematical correction to the accepted construction is required.

## Disposition and credit

Record **30000773 / OWR-1543-004**, historical queue rank 1226, as a credited prior resolution for the original bounded-degree, ordinary-initialization attracting-edge question, including the triangle. The result is due to Codina Cotar and Debleena Thacker, [Annals of Probability 45(4) (2017), 2655–2706](https://doi.org/10.1214/16-AOP1122). The finite count-vector bound retains its Cotar–Limic attribution. **Zero new proof-search turns; no new solution or priority claim.**

## Complete scoped mathematics

The accepted original target is almost-sure eventual alternation on one edge of a connected bounded-degree simple undirected graph with at least one edge, for arbitrary positive finite reciprocally summable, possibly nonmonotone reinforcement and common finite nonnegative integer initialization. The full mathematical text retains the finite count-vector induction for all finite shifted-summable offset configurations, the summable coercive function and second-largest-count bound, the finite-offset frontier product including its zero-index factor and incremented arrival edge, the n≥1 recurrence and both parity bases, and the confinement domination argument.

Arbitrary real edge-dependent offsets under conditions (6) and (8) remain theorem-cited but not independently proof-certified. The journal proof was unavailable for inspection, so no manuscript/journal identity or journal-error claim is made. Vertex reinforcement, directed edges, and arbitrary unbounded-degree graphs are outside the accepted scope.

Record **30002367 / OWR-12495-007** as a credited prior resolution of Totaro's finite-group mod-p Chow detection/suspension conjecture by **David Hemminger**, Proposition 6.1 with Theorem 5.6 and the coarse Theorem 6.2(a), [Algebraic & Geometric Topology 21(4) (2021), 1881–1910](https://doi.org/10.2140/agt.2021.21.1881). **Zero new target proof-attempt turns; no novelty claim for the target theorem.**

For every finite constant group G, every prime p, and every field k with char(k) different from p containing all pth roots of unity, the centralizer-detection degree of CH^*(BG_k)/p equals its greatest nonzero unstable-module suspension degree. ## Exact negative result

Adds the complete authored proof and substantive independent internal AI mathematical audit for problem 30002112 / OWR-12005-004.

For every fixed integer m>=2, bounded connected smooth domains in R^(m+1) with exactly two connected boundary components defeat every finite pair of dimension-only constants in the additive estimate

lambda_k(boundary Omega) |boundary Omega|^(2/m) <= A_m I(Omega)^(1+2/m) + B_m k^(2/m).

Here I(Omega)=|boundary Omega|/|Omega|^(m/(m+1)); the spectrum is intrinsic Laplace-Beltrami for the induced boundary metric and includes all zero modes and multiplicities, indexed from 1. The quotient with the sum of the two unweighted target terms tends to infinity. The domain itself is connected. No connected-boundary or m=1 result is claimed.

The existence inputs are credited to [Colbois-Dryden-El Soufi, Theorem 1.4 and Section 5](https://arxiv.org/abs/0909.5346), Nash and Kuiper in the [precise C0-dense embedding form](https://www.math.ias.edu/delellis/sites/math.ias.edu.delellis/files/contr_vol_Nash_11.pdf), standard smooth approximation and generalized Jordan-Brouwer separation. The authored argument supplies metric comparison, exact area and high gap in a small ball, a connected cavity domain, exact spherical mode counting and the limiting contradiction. All final boundaries are smooth. In dimension 2 topology may vary; in dimensions at least 3 the inner component may be a sphere.

The [OWR question](https://doi.org/10.4171/owr/2012/33) and [CEG spectrum conventions](https://arxiv.org/abs/1007.0826) were inspected in the accepted audit. Source inspection limits, including Hirsch through CDE rather than separate book retrieval, remain explicit. The complete mathematical proof and all substantive audit sections are unchanged. ## Prior negative resolution of the unrestricted question

Adds the complete elementary reconstruction and substantive independent internal mathematical audit for problem 30002714 / OWR-13351-013. This is a prior published counterexample, with no new theorem, novelty, or historical-priority claim.

For any field k, start from R = k[x,y,z]_(x,y,z) in K = k(x,y,z), with the explicit rank-three lexicographic valuation v(x) = (0,0,1), v(y) = (0,1,0), v(z) = (1,0,0). The exact local quadratic transforms are R_i = k[x,y/x^i,z/x^i]_(x,y/x^i,z/x^i). Their strict infinite union S is nonarchimedean.

The full proof computes S* = S[1/x] = T = R_(y,z) = k(x)[y,z]_(y,z), including denominator normalization at late stages, the fixed nonzero witness y with yT contained in S, and the elementary UFD complete-closure argument. Neither y/z nor z/y lies in T, so T is not a valuation ring in the original fraction field.

Credit remains with Heinzer, Loper, Olberding, Schoutens and Toeniskoetter, [Ideal theory of infinite directed unions of local quadratic transforms](https://arxiv.org/abs/1505.06445v3), Example 7.2 and Theorem 6.9; [Journal of Algebra 474 (2017), 213–239](https://doi.org/10.1016/j.jalgebra.2016.11.014). ## Credited prior negative resolution

For problem 30001214 / OWR-3397-002, the unrestricted maximal-spectrum local-closedness assertion is false: in every integer dimension d >= 4, there is a complex affine integral Poisson algebra A and a maximal ideal m whose symplectic core C(m) is not locally closed in Max A.

The essential existence theorem is prior work of Jason Bell, Stéphane Launois, Omar León Sánchez and Rahim Moosa, [Poisson algebras via model theory and differential-algebraic geometry](https://doi.org/10.4171/JEMS/712), J. Eur. Math. Soc. 19 (2017), 2019–2049. Their Theorem 4.1 supplies a differential domain R of Krull dimension n=d-1. Its Manin-kernel foundations are imported rather than independently reproved. No new counterexample or novelty is claimed.

The complete authored implication reconstructs the polynomial Poisson conversion A=R[t], its fraction-field center, zero intersection of nonzero Poisson primes, the rational-to-primitive argument, density of each primitive maximal-spectrum core, and the exact local-closedness bridge. This supplies a genuine maximal ideal and a non-locally-closed core, rather than stopping at a rational non-locally-closed prime. The dimension relation dim R=n=d-1 and dim A=d is explicit.

The inspected LWW mathematical body is [arXiv:1908.06542v2](https://arxiv.org/abs/1908.06542v2), dated 7 May 2020. Its Theorem 6.7(ii) quantifies over all ordinary prime-spectrum cores. This refutes that overbroad clause in the inspected manuscript.

## Accepted prior resolution

This authored exposition records the exact finite balanced-subsequence-pattern
classification proved by Gal Beniamini, Nir Lavee and Nati Linial in
[*How Balanced Can Permutations Be?*](https://doi.org/10.1007/s00493-024-00127-x),
Combinatorica 45, article 9 (2025). For integers n>=k>=1:

- k=1: every n>=1.
- k=2: n>=2 and n=0 or 1 modulo 4.
- k=3: n>=3 and n=0,1,9,20,28,29 modulo 36.
- k>=4: no n>=k.

This is an audit of a prior published resolution, with no novelty claim.
The pattern definition uses arbitrary increasing index sets. Endpoints,
infinitude for each k<=3, and nonexistence for each k>=4 are included.

## Complete proof and finite-evidence boundary

The elementary increasing-pair square identity gives the positive discrepancy
n(n-1)(2n+5)/72 and a complete contradiction for n>=k>=4. Downward closure,
its endpoints, and elementary order-1/order-2 sufficiency remain self-contained.
Order-3 arithmetic, quarter-turn counting, the odd-centre correction, six
source-attributed analytical families, chamber cuts, and exact finite-sum
polynomial derivations are retained. Their unbounded conclusions do not rely
on interpolation from sampled values.

Full order-3 sufficiency additionally uses premise F1, the 19 separately
checked exceptional witnesses in published Appendix A Table 1, pages 28–29,
equivalently [arXiv:2306.16954v1](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2306.16954v1), Table 1,
page 21. Every list was validated as a permutation and all triples were
counted by two independently written methods. The two source versions agree.
Numerical permutation lists, individual witness outcome tables, raw
certificates and executable code are omitted. The complete low-order
classification cannot be independently reproduced from this edition alone;
this is not a complete self-contained proof of the finite-witness part.
The precise source citation locates the missing evidence. Hashes alone do
not prove it. Reproduction requires obtaining Table 1 and rechecking F1.

## Verification scope and source credit

The accepted audit independently checked the pair-square identity on all
5,913 permutations of lengths 1–7 and the rotation formulas on 306
parity-labelled inputs of lengths 1–5. It checked all six families using
exact chamber inequalities and polynomial summation, as well as finite
direct tests. Historical normal, -O and -OO runs produced byte-identical
substantive output. This edition preparation byte-authenticated that
evidence; it performed no new mathematical computation or source inspection.
Source titles, public URLs, PDF hashes and sizes, and historical retrieval
and inspection metadata are provided without copying source text.

Acceptance covers the historical exact target only, not the paper's unrelated
quantitative discrepancy, permuton or reconstruction claims. The endpoint,
odd-centre and chamber derivations are explanatory completions, not a claim
that the published theorem is false. This AI-assisted exposition is unrefereed.
Acceptance means an independent internal AI audit. No external human peer
review, formal proof-assistant certification, CI verification, novelty or
exhaustive literature-status claim is made.

Exactly eight authored proof/audit/acceptance/provenance/verification files
are added under unsolved_math_prioritization/attempts/3100034. QUEUE.md and
all unrelated paths are unchanged. Copied sources, numerical witness data,
raw certificates, executable code and private coordination material are excluded.
